fields.submission-description:
Agentonomy Commerce lets AI agents purchase services and retrieve results within a budget explicitly authorized by the user. One MCP interface connects service discovery, fixed quotes, spending controls, independently verified payment, delivery and recovery.

Core controls wallet identity, signed spending mandates, policy and risk checks, budget reservations and audit. The Monad rail adds a user-signed EIP-712 SpendGrant and an ERC-20 executor enforcing the token, payee, execution signer, per-payment and total caps, expiry, revocation and replay protection. Each purchase has a separate Core execution authorization. A watcher checks the transaction, receipt, payment and transfer events, and a canonical finality boundary through two RPC observations before Core accepts settlement.

The Monad testnet implementation has now been deployed and exercised on chain 10143. An OKX owner completed identity verification, the business mandate, the EIP-712 budget grant and finite 1.00 TestUSD allowance. An actual clink_node MCP purchase paid 0.30 TestUSD. After a transport interruption, recovery of the original paid order delivered a CSV reconciliation report: income 10.00 USD, expense 2.00 USD, net 8.00 USD. Repeating recovery and query returned the same order, report and payment, with one delivery and 0.70 TestUSD remaining.

Payment evidence: https://testnet.monadexplorer.com/tx/0x2711ae051fbf132e544e984c11db6b3b8b518caa40a70d380520743159408037 . The successful receipt in block 68984424 was independently verified by Core and its watcher through two RPCs. The token and executor deployment evidence is in docs/monad/role-session-acceptance.md. TestUSD has no monetary value and is not official USDC.

Current access boundary: the real Monad operator UI, API and HTTP merchant run on loopback. https://review.agentonomy.xyz/ is a separate, explicitly simulated demonstration. The public live Monad product URL, owner-wallet revocation acceptance and recorded videos remain pending.

The repository is self-contained: Core, Marketplace and Node are copied first-party Clink components, with necessary Monad adapters and recovery extensions. Imported code and new hackathon work are identified in source-baseline and acceptance documents. AI coding assistance was used. Validated implementation commit: 32f0211dc4efc0c602c990b4171da67cc51f0eb3. No external audit, customer adoption or revenue is claimed.

Built by Agentonomy. Website: https://agentonomy.xyz/
fields.submission-goToMarket:
Our initial users are developers building AI agents that need to purchase small, clearly scoped digital services without giving an agent unrestricted control over a wallet. Our first merchant example is a deterministic CSV reconciliation service with a fixed quote and a verifiable delivered result.

We plan to acquire developers through a reproducible repository, a short local quickstart, the MCP integration and an accessible demo. Monad developer communities and hackathon feedback will be the first distribution channels. We will invite a small number of agent builders and API providers to test the complete budget-to-delivery flow, document integration friction and publish corrected examples. These are planned pilots, not existing partnerships or customers.

For merchants, we will provide an integration guide covering service discovery, immutable quotes, payment verification, delivery and recovery. The initial scope is fixed-price digital services where both the charge and the result can be checked. We will expand only after the first integrations reliably complete purchases and recover failures.

We will measure time to first successful purchase, completed-purchase and delivery rates, recovery without duplicate charges, repeat developer usage and retained merchant integrations. Our planned business model is hosted infrastructure and support for service providers, with pricing tested after early pilots. We do not currently claim users, revenue or paid adoption.
fields.submission-oneLiner: Let AI agents reliably purchase services and retrieve results within user-authorized budgets.
